fact_claims.verbatim: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year
the flagship model rate was 6.4 per 100,000
Three thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator.
The flagship’s 55 °C sustained-heat test failure rate was 6.2%.
Remote emergency shut-off is supported by 38% of installed units.
Built-in fire suppression would cost about $42 per unit to add.
Halcyon’s Ember 8 had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
while its 55 °C test failure rate was 3.9%

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account and available unit/model and location information. Affected customers shall be notified within 48 hours when the incident presents a potential safety risk to their unit or requires inspection, shutdown, or other action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Before market placement and at least annually thereafter, each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-accepted protocol and representative units. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% for any model. Individual per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public. Regulators may set a reasonable deadline for corrective action and retesting, and may restrict sales where corrective action is inadequate, deadlines are not met, or an imminent serious risk exists.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off accessible to the customer and authorized emergency responders, with safeguards against unauthorized activation. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to support remote shut-off, where technically feasible, within 72 months after adoption; where retrofitting is infeasible, they shall provide customers an equivalent documented emergency isolation method and notify them of its limitations.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-accepted performance and reliability protocol. The requirement does not preclude regulators from requiring earlier measures for a model presenting an imminent serious risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall immediately notify regulators and affected customers, submit an incident investigation and corrective-action plan, and implement any interim safety measures required by the regulator. The regulator shall promptly assess the evidence and may require a recall or other proportionate corrective action; it shall order an immediate recall where evidence indicates an imminent serious risk.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict: all thermal incidents are reportable within 24 hours, and customers must be notified within 48 hours for potential safety risks. S2 keeps the 5% limit and gives purchasers/regulators access to per-model results while avoiding public publication and allowing corrective action before sales restrictions. S3 sets new-unit shut-off at 24 months and retrofit at 72 months with an equivalent isolation fallback; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 triggers mandatory notification/investigation at 8/100k but leaves recall to regulator discretion, with immediate recall only for imminent serious risk.
